40b4a3598da1364e4d6ec9d1c8ff8ee01cbc347c.summary: IBM X-Force IRIS tracks ITG07, a threat actor that has intruded into geographically dispersed transportation-sector organizations over nine months. IRIS says ITG07 most closely aligns with activity other vendors call Chafer or APT39, which Symantec describes as an alleged Iran-based group. The report details a custom backdoor IRIS named TREKX, which NCCGroup reported in March 2019 as Chafer activity. ITG07 also uses legacy tools such as a custom Mimikatz, NBTScan, PsExec, webshells and remote access via Citrix, RDP and SSH-based tools. IRIS says ITG07 appears mainly engaged in surveillance…

40b21146d8883a66532a724f0e847cb1cc39e3d5.summary: NTT Security Japan's SOC describes Operation RestyLink, an APT campaign targeting Japanese companies, first observed in mid-April 2022. The report thinks it may have started in March 2022, with a related attack possibly around October 2021. Delivery used spear phishing, ZIP and LNK files, decoy PDFs, Word startup-folder persistence and DLL sideloading, with Cobalt Strike and possibly Covenant. The report names DarkHotel as the strongest suspect among four candidate APT groups but says there is no convincing evidence to confirm attribution.

40ab002e9b537d70074e1670e13274caf9c445e7.summary: This is an index page for the Chrysaor malware family, which the page attributes to Fraunhofer FKIE and which is also known as Pegasus. It has no description of its own. It lists about 150 titles of articles, blog posts, reports and tweets about Chrysaor, dated from 2016 to 2024, from security vendors, researchers, civil society groups and news outlets. It is a bibliography, not a threat report, so no facts are recorded.

407423e2af3d2bd6c14f2b254f19759f23e8edaa.summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz blog, published 2023-09-12, attributing activity to APT36. It describes Linux desktop entry files as a new, low-volume attack vector. The first case, in May 2023, was a credential phishing site targeting Indian government staff, with ZIP archives carrying a decoy PDF. Later samples used decoy PDFs and payloads identified as Mythic Poseidon binaries, with C2 panels on two servers. The report says some payloads were still in development at analysis time.

4080fd3fa1acb8cfe0939242f6d2cf32478dccf3.summary: Aqua's Team Nautilus research team reports fileless malware that runs from memory in container images. Four Docker Hub images were found designed for this, and two Docker Hub accounts are linked to the TeamTNT group. The malware hides processes with a rootkit, runs a crypto miner from memory, and leaves a backdoor. The report names Tsunami malware as a component, describes packing as a way to evade scanners, and recommends image scanning, minimal privileges, runtime detection and log review.
